strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: clearly articulates three fundamental limitations of layer-wise reconstruction approaches that are compelling and well-presented
Impressive empirical results: achieves 90% sparsity across multiple architectures (OPT, Gemma, LLaMA) with consistent 5-30× improvements in perplexity over state-of-the-art at high sparsity
Strong downstream task performance: maintains 6.06%p average accuracy advantage at 90% sparsity across 7 zero-shot tasks, demonstrating robust generalization
Solid theoretical grounding: provides rigorous convergence analysis for both ELSA and ELSA-L with proper treatment of quantization effects in the proofs
Technical innovations: objective-aware projection using Fisher information is clever, well-motivated, and efficiently leverages existing optimizer states from Adam
Comprehensive experimental validation: covers multiple scales (125M-27B), architectures, sparsity levels (50-90%), and adaptations to different sparsity patterns (N:M, non-uniform)
Scalability demonstrated: ELSA-L enables pruning at 27B scale with 66% memory footprint reduction, showing practical applicability to larger models
Thorough ablations: demonstrate value of both objective choice (NTP vs REM) and objective-aware projection, with gains increasing at higher sparsity levels
weaknesses: Missing practical efficiency metrics: no wall-clock time comparisons during pruning despite ADMM requiring 4096 iterative steps; no actual inference latency/throughput measurements on hardware

Hyperparameter selection lacks guidance: Table 5 shows dramatic variation in learning rates (1e-5 to 2e-1) and penalties across models; no principled approach for selecting hyperparameters for new models or limited sensitivity analysis

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: identifies why layer-wise fails but provides limited insight into why surrogate-free formulation specifically enables 90% sparsity versus other possible mechanisms
Weak theoretical guarantees: convergence to λ-stationary points only, not global optima; no characterization of solution quality relative to other methods or sample complexity analysis

Inconsistent moderate-sparsity performance: ELSA sometimes underperforms at 50-60% sparsity (Table 6: OPT-1.3B 50% is 19.66 vs 16.38 for SAFE); insufficient explanation of this trade-off and when to use ELSA
Limited ablation of technical choices: diagonal Hessian approximation is aggressive but alternatives not explored; ablation only tests projection on/off rather than different variants
Scope limitations: all experiments on transformer LLMs only; generalization to RNNs, MoE models, diffusion models unclear; evaluation limited to primarily English next-token prediction
Defensive memory analysis: discussion argues layer-wise methods don't save memory but lacks concrete numerical comparisons; memory claims may be overstated
Incomplete non-uniform analysis: Table 2 only compares evolutionary methods at 70% sparsity; finding that uniform ELSA beats optimized non-uniform allocation deserves deeper investigation
Opaque computational cost: practical pruning time compared to one-shot baselines is unclear despite claimed efficiency advantages

strengths: Clearly identifies and articulates three specific limitations of existing layer-wise reconstruction error minimization approaches (error compounding, sequential suboptimality, surrogate objective mismatch)
Principled methodological contribution: formulates pruning as proper constrained optimization and solves via ADMM, moving beyond heuristic-based approaches
Dramatic empirical improvements at extreme sparsity: 10-100× better perplexity than baselines at 90% sparsity across all tested models
Comprehensive experimental validation: 6 models (125M-27B), multiple sparsity levels, zero-shot tasks, extreme sparsity (99%), practical speedups (3.98×) and memory savings (7.80×)
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating importance of objective choice (NTP vs REM) and objective-aware projection, validating design decisions
Theoretical convergence guarantees provided for both ELSA and ELSA-L, even with quantization
Scalability demonstrated on 27B models with memory-efficient ELSA-L variant (55% memory reduction)
Strong reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, and code release commitment
weaknesses: Significant computational cost (7.12 GPU-hours on 4× A100s for LLaMA-2-7B at 90%) limits practical adoption; 28-44× more expensive than one-shot methods despite arguing for quality-cost tradeoff
Hyperparameter tuning complexity requires extensive per-model and per-sparsity configuration (learning rates: 5e-5 to 2e-4, λ: 1e-4 to 5e-2, schedule changes); limited guidance for new settings

Limited analysis of why surrogate-free optimization works: unclear whether improvement stems from eliminating surrogate, global joint optimization, or penalty formulation; ablation separating these factors would strengthen claims
Structured sparsity results (N:M patterns) show no advantage over baselines, suggesting method benefits only unstructured sparsity and limiting hardware deployment scenarios
Calibration data requirement (32,768 points) is 256× more than baselines; scaling behavior not thoroughly analyzed
Convergence to λ-stationary points rather than global optima is weaker guarantee for non-convex setting; solution quality assessment missing
Hardware and kernel dependence: inference gains rely on specific MACKO sparse multiplication; results not validated on other sparse kernels or hardware
Modest real-world usability despite perplexity gains: zero-shot accuracy at 90% sparsity (38.52%) remains far below dense (59.67%), raising questions about practical deployment
Baseline comparisons at extreme sparsity (95-99%) limited to Wanda with fine-tuning; matched compute budget comparisons would strengthen claims
